marker: # ref_size is the product length measured in the SCHU S4 assembly GCA_000008985.1 (AJ749949.2) by in
# silico PCR with these primers, outer primer edge to outer primer edge. The publication's Genomic
# location column prints the end coordinate abbreviated, giving only the digits that differ from the
# start (1886647-7109 means 1886647-1887109). That rule was checked against all 25 rows of the table and
# the decoded span equals the measured product for 24 of them, which confirms both the decoding and that
# the column is the amplicon, outer primer edge to outer primer edge, not the repeat array.
# The published start coordinates are offset from AJ749949.2 by 16 to 60 bases while the spans match
# exactly, so the table's coordinates come from a different release of the sequence than this assembly.
# Ft-M10 is the one span that disagrees. The cell reads 1283441-4086 and decodes to 646 bp, which is not
# a transcription or decoding error, but the assembly yields only one possible product of 617 bp: the
# forward primer occurs once and no other reverse site lies in range. The 29 base difference is not a
# multiple of the 16 bp unit, so it is either a real difference between this assembly and the sequence
# used in 2004 or a mis-stated end coordinate in the source. The measured 617 is used, because ref_size
# has to describe the assembly the calls are anchored on.
# unit_length, ref_repeats and patterns are not published in the supplied table. They are filled from
# the reference only where the array is strong enough to trust (3 or more copies, 95
# per cent or better TRF match, unit of 5 bp or more, and the mlvatyper tandem count equal to
# the TRF count). 16 of 25 markers qualify and can be called; the other 9 are
# sized but report NO_DEFINITION until values are taken from the publication's marker characteristics
# table. Alleles are therefore anchored on SCHU S4 as measured here and are not guaranteed to match the
# allele names used in the publication.

#   filled: Ft-M2 6bp x5; Ft-M3 9bp x21; Ft-M4 5bp x3; Ft-M5 16bp x3; Ft-M6 21bp x3; Ft-M7 16bp x4; Ft-M8 16bp x4; Ft-M9 16bp x4; Ft-M10 16bp x18; Ft-M14 6bp x5; Ft-M15 6bp x3; Ft-M16 10bp x3; Ft-M17 6bp x4; Ft-M18 6bp x5; Ft-M20 12bp x3; Ft-M21 7bp x3
#   not filled: Ft-M1 (2 copies); Ft-M11 (2 copies); Ft-M12 (2 copies); Ft-M13 (2 copies); Ft-M19 (0 copies); Ft-M22 (77% match); Ft-M23 (2 copies); Ft-M24 (2 copies); Ft-M25 (2 bp unit)
# The derived unit lengths were tested across strains. A locus keeps the same flanking length in
# every strain, so the sizes of its product must differ by whole multiples of its repeat unit.
# Amplifying this panel in seven Francisella genomes, SCHU S4, LVS, OSU18, WY96-3418, FSC198,
# NE061598 and TI0902, confirms 15 of the 16 filled units: every observed step at those loci is a
# whole number of units. Ft-M8 is the exception and its steps, 15 and 33 bases, are not multiples
# of its 16 bp unit, so a product of that locus from another strain can give a fractional allele,
# which the caller flags INTERMEDIATE rather than reporting a whole number. The cause is the shared
# repeat family described below: in WY96-3418 the Ft-M8 product comes from a position about 1.85 Mb
# away from where it lies in the other genomes, so the primers have selected a different member of
# the family rather than the array they amplify in SCHU S4. Read an Ft-M8 allele with that in mind.
# The same test also matches these loci to the other bundled Francisella scheme. Its names are
# padded, Ft-M02 against Ft-M2 here, and the units derived independently there agree with the ones
# derived here at Ft-M2, Ft-M3, Ft-M4, Ft-M5, Ft-M6, Ft-M10 and Ft-M20, which confirms that the
# padded and unpadded names are the same VNTR. The two schemes use different primer pairs and
# different references, so their sizes and alleles are not interchangeable.
# Ft-M5, Ft-M7, Ft-M8, Ft-M9 and Ft-M10 share the reverse primer and also share one 16 bp repeat unit,
# AAAAAGATATTTGTAG, at five unrelated positions, so they sample one repeat family rather than five
# independent loci. That oligo occurs 50 times in SCHU S4 inside a conserved element of at least 220 bp,
# so each product is selected by size alone.
